parties:
Sogra Begum   ------ Appellant
Vs.
Commissioner of Taxes  ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
2. It is stated that the petitioner is a pardahnashin lady and a housewife and she was assessed to tax under section 82(2)/93 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 1984 on total income of Taka 11,61,555.00 for the assessment year 1987-88 and being aggrieved by the aforesaid assessment order an appeal was preferred before the Additional Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) who had granted relief to the petitioner and deleted the addition of Taka 10,07,205.00 against which the department preferred a second appeal before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal which by its order dated 1-8-99 set aside the first appellate order of the Additional Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) and restored the order of the DCT. It is further stated that the Tribunal communicated the said order to the petitioner on 29-11-99 when she had a massive heart attack and she was also not keeping good health seeing the murder of her husband and the aforesaid order was misplaced by her which was however re-traced by her subsequently and handed over the same to her lawyer on 26-3-2000. Thereafter, an application was filed before the Tribunal under section 173 of the Ordinance, 1984 for rectification as the order itself was a mistake on the very face of it as the investment in the year 1968 to 1986 cannot be income during the income year 1987-88. So, on the good belief the petitioner preferred to file an application under section 173 of the Ordinance for rectification of the order of the Appellate Tribunal and ultimately, that application being Miscellaneous Application No. 58 of 1999-2000 was dismissed by the Tribunal vide order dated 4-5-2000 and the said order was communicated on 31-5-2000. The petitioner being aggrieved by the said order of Appellate Tribunal passed in the aforesaid Miscellaneous case now intends to file a reference application under section 160 of the Ordinance before this Court against the order dated 1-8-99 passed by the Tribunal in ITA No. 1234 of 1997-98 (Assessment year 1987-88). The assessee received the copy of the order passed in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case on 31-5-2000 and the application for condonation of delay was filed on 1-8-2000. 

 3. Mr Md Altaf Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the assessee petitioner, submits that the petitioner was prevented by sufficient cause in preferring the reference application before this Court under section 160 of the Ordinance against the order passed by the Tribunal in ITA No. 1234 of 1999-2000 on 1-8-99 inasmuch as she was misled by ill advice of her lawyer to file an application for rectification before the Tribunal under section 173 of the Ordinance as the mistake was apparent on the face of the record. The learned Advocate further submits that a litigant should not be punished for the negligence committed by the lawyer or for the ill advice of the Advocate. The learned Advocate further submits that in dealing with a condonation application the principle that substantial justice shall take preponderance over technical consideration should always be kept in view in deciding whether the petitioner was prevented by sufficient cause for the delay and in support of his contention he relies on the decision reported in 51 DLR (AD) 253 and the decision reported in 167 ITR 471 decision of the Indian Supreme Court. The learned Advocate also submitted that the instant case is covered by the provisions of section 14 of the Limitation Act inasmuch as the application filed under section 173 of the Ordinance was before a wrong forum. 

 4. Perused the application and considered the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. In this application the clear case that has been made out by the petitioner is that being aggrieved by the assessment order dated 23-11-95 passed by the Assistant Commissioner of Taxes for the assessment year 1987-88 the petitioner preferred an appeal before the Additional Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) who allowed the appeal in part and deleted a substantial amount to the tune of Taka 10 lakh and odd but the department being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of the Additional Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) took a Second Appeal before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal being ITA No. 1234 of 1997-98 (Assessment year 1987-88) and the Tribunal after hearing the parties allowed the appeal and set aside the order of the Additional Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) and restored the order of the ACT. This order of the Tribunal was duly communicated to the assessee petitioner on 29-11-99 but that was a point of time when she had a massive heart attack and she was also not otherwise keeping good health since the murder of her husband in the heart of the city. Further contention of the petitioner is that the aforesaid order was misplaced by the petitioner and ultimately handed it over to her lawyer on 26-3-2000. It thus appears that the order was retraced by the petitioner but at what point of time that has not been disclosed in this petition but it is clear that on 26-3-2000 that order was handed over to the learned Advocate who on an examination of the same advised her to file an application for rectification of that order under section 173 of the Ordinance instead of filing a reference application under section 160 of the Ordinance before this Court and accordingly, an application was filed under the aforesaid section of the Ordinance which was registered as Miscellaneous Application No. 58 of 1999-2000. The Tribunal after hearing the petitioner dismissed that application on 4-5-2000 and communicated the said order to the petitioner on 31-5-2000 and now having failed before the Tribunal in her application under section 173 of the Ordinance she wants to prefer a reference application under section 160 of the Ordinance against the order of the Tribunal dated 1-8-99 passed in ITA No. 1234 of 97-98. It thus appears that on examination of the Tribunal's order dated 1-8-1999 the petitioner in her wisdom decided to file an application under section 173 of the Ordinance for rectification of the said order of the Tribunal rather than filing the reference application before this Court under section 160 of the Ordinance. It is clear that against that order she had two remedies available to her, i.e. to call in question the legality and propriety of the order of the Tribunal under section 160 of the Ordinance. It is clear that against that order she had two remedies available to her i.e. to call in question the legality and propriety of the order of the Tribunal under section 160 of the Ordinance before this Court by way of reference application or she could file an application before the Tribunal under section 173 of the Ordinance for rectification of the order of the mistake as the mistake was apparent on the face of it. 

 5. Now the question, that calls for determination in this application is that in view of the admitted facts and circumstances of the case can it be said that the petitioner was prevented by sufficient cause in filing this reference application before this Court in time? From the facts noted above it is clear that the application under section 173 of the Ordinance was filed before the correct forum. Thus, the question of getting benefit of section 14 of the Limitation Act does not arise at all. Moreover, the instant reference application is not against the order dated 31-5-2000 passed in Miscellaneous Application No. 58 of 1999-2000. Rather, this is against the original order of the Tribunal dated 1-8-99 passed in ITA No. 1234 of 1997/1998 (Assessment year 1987-88). 

 7. In view of these facts and circumstances it cannot be said that the petitioner was prevented by sufficient cause in filing the reference application in time. The petitioner voluntarily decided to seek her remedy under section 173 of the Ordinance rather than filing a reference under section 160 of the Ordinance. After failing in her attempt made under section 173 of the Ordinance now the petitioner wants to fall back on section 160 of the Ordinance to attack the order dated 1-8-99 on merit. If now the petitioner is allowed to file a reference application after rejection of the application filed under section 173 of the Ordinance, on 4-5-2000, the petitioner will be given a long latitude, in other words, she will have lots of both the worlds. Such a course is not allowed by the Ordinance. Even in civil Courts if any ex parte decree is passed against a defendant he can either file an application under Order 9 rule 13 for setting aside the ex parte decree and/or file an appeal before the higher Court. The only limitation is that if the appeal is heard first the Order 9 rule 13 application becomes incompetent i.e. the jurisdiction to pass orders on an application under the Rule subsists only so long as the appellate Court does not decide the appeal. Similarly, in the instant case also the petitioner could resort to both the remedies simultaneously and decision in one would render the other infructuous. But in the present case the assessee giving a go-by to one remedy jumped on the other on her own and when it was proved futile she wants to resort to the other and such course of action is not permissible under the law. In the premises, therefore, the petitioner cannot be allowed to file a reference application now after being unsuccessful in her attempt before the Tribunal under section 173 of the Ordinance. 

 8. There is another aspect of the case. This is an application for condonation of delay. It is now well settled that each day's delay has to be explained. In this case the petitioner has utterly failed to explain each day's delay satisfactorily inasmuch as the impugned order was communicated to her on 29-11-99 but when it was misplaced is not mentioned. There is no indication when the said order was retraced. It is only stated that the said order was handed over to her lawyer on 26-3-2000. When the Miscellaneous Case No. 58 of 1999-2000 was filed is also not disclosed. From the records it is found that the said Miscellaneous Case was rejected on 4-5-2000 and the present application was filed on 1-8-2000. It further appears that the result of the Miscellaneous Case was communicated to the petitioner on 31-5-2000 but what happened in between 31-5-2000 and 1-8-2000 is not explained. The petitioner has not made any attempt to explain the delay not to speak of each day's delay. On this score also the application is liable to be rejected. 

 9. We have gone through the decision relied on by the learned Advocate for the petitioner and we are in respectful agreement with the principles laid down in those decisions. But in the facts and circumstances of the case they have no manner of application. The facts of instant case are quite distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the aforesaid two cases. In the instant case the petitioner in the garb of filing an application for condonation of delay, in fact, wants to avail of two remedies against the same order. We are of the opinion that the assessee cannot be given two opportunities to assail the self-same order and in that view of the matter we do not find any materials on record to arrive at a finding that the petitioner was, in fact, prevented by sufficient cause in filing the reference application under section 160 of the Ordinance within the prescribed time. 

 10. The petitioner at her peril had chosen to file an application under section 173 of the Ordinance rather than to file a reference application before this Court under section 160 of the Ordinance. It is now well settled that he who chooses the sword must perish by the sword. In that view of the matter the petitioner must not be allowed to fall back on section 160 of the Ordinance after being unsuccessful in Miscellaneous Application No. 58 of 1998. 

 At this stage the learned Advocate for the petitioner makes a prayer for giving a certificate under section 162 of the Ordinance for filing an appeal before the Appellate Division. In the judgment we have discussed in detail the facts and circumstances of the case to show how the petitioner has miserably failed to make out a case for condonation of delay. Thus, it does not appear to us to be a fit case for granting a certificate as prayed for. Hence the prayer is rejected.
